S1 repaired-watchtower: Pale new oak scarfed onto charred black legs at half height: the one tower the banner rebuilt,
the seam plain from the yard.
S2 weathered-fortification: The west palisade leans outward on rotten feet, propped with stakes; its tower is soft
S3 weathered-fortification: A grassed bank and charred post stumps: the earlier holders' outer ring, half ploughed
S4 levy-yard-vs-noble-architecture: A turf levy house and a kerbed mound on a terrace below the palisade; far up the
valley on the opposite shoulder, the allied Great House's barrow-hall among colossal stones.
S5 merchant-road: The valley road crosses at the ford under the horn post and climbs to the gate: drovers, traders and
the Blood-Throne's riders all use it.
S6 unfinished-structure: Posts and roof trees raised for a guest hall, scaffolded, with sheer-legs standing idle
S7 ceremonial-place: Eight carved posts round the hearth with bare iron hooks waiting for recognised honours.
S8 empty-character-position: The nominated representative's stone before the file stones, occupied or empty according
S9 older-house-ruin: A longhouse left when its family followed the previous holders away; the roof has fallen in at
S10 ancestral-memory: A ring of standing stones raised by an older people on a ledge at the foot of the fell; the path
to them is worn deeper than any lane inside the palisade.
S11 ancestral-memory: A byre built for beasts far larger than cattle, its door twice the longhall's height, and an
arch of enormous ribs over the byre gate.
S12 class-contrast: Carved stave walls and a curved roof for the eldest family, a half-sunk pit-house with a fallen
corner against the bank, the longhall over both.
S13 water-memory: The spring that never freezes, in the saddle under the fell; water carriers pass through the postern
S14 boundary-dispute: Two boundary stones a stride apart at the end of the field track, where the downstream farms
